title: Exploring the impact of ChatGPT: conversational AI in education
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the growing use of ChatGPT in education and asks what benefits and challenges it presents, how it affects student engagement and learning outcomes, what ethical safeguards are needed, and how it changes educators’ roles. The authors position the study as a systematic literature review of recent research on conversational AI in educational contexts, motivated by the rapid uptake of ChatGPT and concerns about both its instructional promise and its risks.

The approach is a systematic literature review following Kitchenham and Charters’ SLR process and aligned with PRISMA reporting guidance. The authors searched multiple databases including IEEE Xplore, Springer, Elsevier ScienceDirect, ACM Digital Library, and SSRN using ChatGPT- and AI-related search terms. From an initial pool of approximately 729 records, they applied inclusion/exclusion criteria and quality assessment rules to select 70 papers published between 2022 and 2023. They then used thematic analysis to synthesize findings across studies.

The review is not centered on a single participant sample or one implemented intervention. Instead, it synthesizes studies concerning ChatGPT users in educational settings, especially students and teachers, and also discusses issues relevant to parents and educational institutions. Contexts span education broadly rather than a single level or country, with the review focusing on how ChatGPT is used as a conversational AI tool for tutoring, feedback, information access, writing support, and instructional assistance.

The main conclusions are that ChatGPT can enhance learning, improve access to information, support personalized assistance, increase engagement through rapid feedback and interactive dialogue, and help foster critical thinking when used appropriately. At the same time, the review highlights major concerns including bias, inaccurate responses, privacy and data protection, academic integrity, lack of emotional intelligence, and overreliance on AI. The authors conclude that responsible adoption requires clear guidelines, human supervision, teacher awareness, student critical evaluation skills, and ongoing ethical oversight. They also argue that ChatGPT shifts educators’ roles from content delivery toward facilitation, guidance, and personalized support.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: An OpenAI conversational large language model used as an AI chatbot for natural-language interaction, question answering, feedback, and personalized assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied at the review level as the focal conversational AI tool in education, synthesizing literature on its benefits, challenges, effects on student engagement and learning outcomes, ethical safeguards, and implications for educators' roles.

findings.finding_summary: Across the 70 papers included in this systematic review, ChatGPT was synthesized as enhancing learning by providing personalized assistance, interactive support, and improved access to information. The review reports that students can receive tailored responses, prompt feedback, and rapid access to relevant knowledge, which were described as supporting improved learning experiences; no aggregate effect size was reported.
findings.measure: Narrative synthesis of reported learning enhancement, personalized assistance, and information accessibility in reviewed education studies

findings.finding_summary: The review concludes that ChatGPT can enhance student engagement by creating interactive learning environments, encouraging active participation, and supporting reflective thinking and critical thinking development. These findings are presented as qualitative synthesis across the reviewed literature rather than pooled quantitative estimates.
findings.measure: Narrative synthesis of student engagement, participation, reflective thinking, and critical thinking outcomes in reviewed studies

findings.finding_summary: The paper synthesizes that integrating ChatGPT shifts educators' roles from content delivery toward facilitation, guidance, and support for personalized and differentiated learning. At the same time, the review highlights institutional and ethical concerns including bias, inaccuracy, privacy, transparency, and the need for human supervision, training, and policy safeguards.
findings.measure: Narrative synthesis of educator role change, ethical concerns, privacy, bias, and governance recommendations

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic literature review of 70 papers, but it reports narrative thematic synthesis without pooled quantitative effect sizes or a formal meta-analysis. The evidence summarized is therefore useful but methodologically heterogeneous and largely qualitative.
impact_tier_rationale: The review reports generally positive impacts on engagement and learning, but no aggregate effect sizes or confidence intervals are provided. As a result, impact appears promising but remains unclear in magnitude.
